desc:
There are n machines in a row; machine i holds machines[i] items. The work proceeds in rounds. In each round you may choose any number of machines, and every chosen machine passes one of the items it held at the start of the round to one adjacent machine (left or right, your choice per machine). All passes of a round happen at the same time, so an item that has just arrived cannot be passed on in the same round.

Return the minimum number of rounds after which all machines hold the same number of items, or -1 if that cannot be done.

machines = [1,0,5]  -> 3
machines = [0,3,0]  -> 2
machines = [0,2,0]  -> -1
hints: Equal loads need a total divisible by n. Then every machine has a known target.
Fix a machine i. Items have to cross it from the left part to the right part or the other way round. Count how many the left side and the right side are off from their targets.

A machine passes at most one item per round. If both sides lack items, machine i must send out |L| + |R| items in total, one per round. Otherwise the larger of the two imbalances is the bottleneck. The answer is the maximum over all machines.
editorial: Let avg = total / n (answer -1 if not divisible). For machine i let L be (items on its left) minus (i * avg), and R be (items on its right) minus ((n - 1 - i) * avg). A negative value means that side is short of items and needs them to flow in.

If both L < 0 and R < 0, machine i alone has to supply both sides and, as it can emit only one item per round, needs at least -L - R rounds. In every other case the flow across each boundary needs at least |L| and |R| rounds, since one item crosses a boundary per round. Each of these is a lower bound and the largest bound over all machines is attainable, so the answer is max(...) over i. One pass with running sums, O(n).
solution:
def minRoundsToBalance(machines):
    n = len(machines)
    total = sum(machines)
    if total % n:
        return -1
    avg = total // n
    left = 0
    ans = 0
    for i, x in enumerate(machines):
        right = total - left - x
        l = left - i * avg
        r = right - (n - 1 - i) * avg
        if l < 0 and r < 0:
            need = -l - r
        else:
            need = max(abs(l), abs(r))
        ans = max(ans, need)
        left += x
    return ans
